project.name: tack
project.description: Go TUI for GitHub issue/project/shipment workflows, built on Charmbracelet Bubble Tea.

nodes.name: sync-skills-catalog.py
nodes.summary: Per-project installer that clones the kumo-skills-catalog repo and symlinks selected skills into .agents/skills with matching slash-command stubs in .claude/commands.
nodes.languageNotes: Standalone CLI: parses skill SKILL.md frontmatter, manages a manifest of selected skills, and updates .gitignore entries for symlinks.

nodes.name: AGENTS.md
nodes.summary: Short orientation note pointing AI agents at CONTRIBUTING.md and core conventions for the tack repo.

nodes.name: CONTRIBUTING.md
nodes.summary: Contributor guide covering local setup, build/test commands, and code style for the tack Go project.

nodes.name: Makefile
nodes.summary: Build automation defining targets for building, testing, installing, and running the tack binary.

nodes.name: SETUP.md
nodes.summary: End-user setup guide explaining configuration of GitHub access, focus list, and Notion/Hibana integrations needed to run tack.

nodes.name: config.yaml
nodes.summary: Default tack runtime configuration: GitHub project URL, status field name, team roster, and focus issues that drive the board view.

nodes.name: notion-integration.md
nodes.summary: Design and operational notes for the Notion-backed planning integration, including auth, sync semantics, and conflict handling.

nodes.name: promote-ship-workflow.md
nodes.summary: Detailed walkthrough of the elevate/ship workflow: how issues get promoted to shipments, session repo handling, and recovery on attach failure.

nodes.name: go.mod
nodes.summary: Go module manifest declaring the github.com/autumnust/tack module and pinning third-party dependencies (Bubble Tea, Cobra, Redis, etc.).

nodes.name: go.sum
nodes.summary: Go module checksum lockfile pinning exact versions of every transitive dependency.

nodes.name: cache.go
nodes.summary: On-disk JSON cache for fetched GitHub project state, keyed by project URL with a focus-hash guard so changing the focus list invalidates stale snapshots.
nodes.languageNotes: Cache identity is (projectURL, focusHash) — Save filters items by focusSet, Load rejects mismatched focus hashes to avoid serving stale snapshots.

nodes.name: CachedProject
nodes.summary: On-disk shape of the per-project cache: fetch timestamp, project metadata, items, and the focus-set hash that scoped the snapshot.

nodes.name: Save
nodes.summary: Filters project items to those in focus (or with a focused parent) and writes a CachedProject JSON file with the focus hash recorded.

nodes.name: Load
nodes.summary: Loads a cached project snapshot only if it matches the requested focus hash and is fresher than maxAge.

nodes.name: LoadAny
nodes.summary: Loads the cached project ignoring age but still requiring the focus hash to match.

nodes.name: IsFresh
nodes.summary: Reports whether a cached snapshot exists, matches focus, and is younger than maxAge.

nodes.name: hashFocus
nodes.summary: Computes a deterministic SHA-256 hash of the focus set used to tag cache files for invalidation.

nodes.name: cache_test.go
nodes.summary: Unit tests covering cache round-trip, focus filtering, focus-hash invalidation, and expiry semantics for the cache package.

nodes.name: client.go
nodes.summary: Thin GitHub API client wrapping `gh auth token` for credentials and exposing GraphQL and REST helpers used by queries and mutations.
nodes.languageNotes: Authentication shells out to the gh CLI rather than handling tokens directly, simplifying credential management.

nodes.name: Client
nodes.summary: GitHub API client holding an http.Client and bearer token, with graphql and RestGet methods.

nodes.name: NewClient
nodes.summary: Constructs a Client by invoking `gh auth token` to obtain credentials.

nodes.name: graphql
nodes.summary: Sends a GraphQL request to api.github.com, parses the envelope, and surfaces both transport and GraphQL errors.

nodes.name: RestGet
nodes.summary: Issues an authenticated GET against the GitHub REST API and returns the raw response body.

nodes.name: client_test.go
nodes.summary: Tests the GitHub client's GraphQL and REST helpers using a custom RoundTripper that intercepts requests and verifies headers/error propagation.

nodes.name: mutations.go
nodes.summary: GraphQL mutation helpers for changing project board state: moving items between status columns, assigning issues, and adding comments.

nodes.name: MoveItem
nodes.summary: Moves a project item to a named status column by resolving the option ID from the project's status field.

nodes.name: AssignIssue
nodes.summary: Assigns a GitHub user (by login) to an issue via the addAssigneesToAssignable mutation.

nodes.name: AddComment
nodes.summary: Posts a comment on an issue using the addComment GraphQL mutation.

nodes.name: queries.go
nodes.summary: GraphQL and REST queries that hydrate the local model: fetches a Projects v2 board, parses items into ProjectItem, and resolves sub-issue parentage.
nodes.languageNotes: Handles paginated GraphQL field-value queries and a separate REST sub-issues endpoint to reconstruct epic/child relationships.

nodes.name: parseProjectURL
nodes.summary: Parses a github.com Projects v2 URL into owner kind (org or user), login, and project number.

nodes.name: FetchProject
nodes.summary: Pages through the Projects v2 GraphQL API to load the full project: fields, options, and all items with field values.

nodes.name: parseItems
nodes.summary: Translates raw GraphQL response data into ProjectItem records, normalizing field values, status, assignees, and labels.

nodes.name: FetchSubIssues
nodes.summary: Calls the GitHub REST sub_issues endpoint for each issue number to discover parent/child issue relationships.

nodes.name: ResolveParentsFromSubIssues
nodes.summary: Stitches sub-issue mappings into the items list, populating Parent references so grouping by epic works.

nodes.name: queries_test.go
nodes.summary: Tests for the GitHub query layer: project URL parsing, GraphQL item parsing, and parent-from-sub-issue resolution.

nodes.name: strategy.go
nodes.summary: Pluggable grouping strategies for the board view: ByEpic groups children under their parent issue, ByLabel groups by labels, plus a person-based grouping helper.

nodes.name: Strategy
nodes.summary: Interface implemented by issue-grouping strategies, exposing a Name and a Group method.

nodes.name: ByEpic
nodes.summary: Strategy implementation that groups items beneath their parent epic and surfaces standalone items separately.

nodes.name: ByLabel
nodes.summary: Strategy implementation that buckets items by their first matching configured label prefix.

nodes.name: GroupByPerson
nodes.summary: Builds per-person groupings of items with focus filtering, multi-assignee fan-out, and team-order preservation for the board view.

nodes.name: strategy_test.go
nodes.summary: Comprehensive tests for ByEpic, ByLabel, and GroupByPerson covering edge cases like focus filtering, multi-assignee fan-out, and team ordering.

nodes.name: planning.go
nodes.summary: Plain-data structs for the planning domain: Plan, FocusItem, SubItem, TodoItem, ScratchNote, MonthlyTarget, and Annotation collections.

nodes.name: types.go
nodes.summary: Core domain types shared across packages: Config (team, focus, planning), Project, ProjectItem, ParentRef, SubIssue, Comment, and grouping records.

nodes.name: Config
nodes.summary: Top-level user configuration: project URL, status field, team roster, focus issues, and embedded planning config.

nodes.name: ProjectItem
nodes.summary: Issue-level record on the project board: status, assignees, labels, parent/sub-issue references, and field values.

nodes.name: Project
nodes.summary: Project board metadata: ID, title, URL, and field/option definitions including the status field.

nodes.name: TeamLogins
nodes.summary: Returns the GitHub login slice extracted from the configured team roster.

nodes.name: FocusSet
nodes.summary: Computes the per-user focus set as a map of issue numbers, optionally scoped by a single login.

nodes.name: DisplayName
nodes.summary: Resolves a user-friendly display name for a given GitHub login from the team roster.

nodes.name: types_test.go
nodes.summary: Unit tests covering Config helpers: TeamLogins, FocusSet, and DisplayName behavior including focus scoping by login.

nodes.name: main.go
nodes.summary: CLI entry point dispatching subcommands for the TUI, recap/stats, conflict resolution, hibana migration, and config loading.
nodes.languageNotes: Hand-rolled subcommand dispatch on os.Args[1]; loads YAML config from a discovered path and wires the TUI plus auxiliary tools.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Top-level entry point: parses arguments, loads config, and dispatches to the TUI or one of the maintenance subcommands.

nodes.name: loadConfig
nodes.summary: Reads YAML config from a path, expanding tildes and validating required fields.

nodes.name: findConfig
nodes.summary: Searches standard locations for a tack config file (env var, cwd, home).

nodes.name: generateRecap
nodes.summary: Builds a recap of recent hibana entries grouped/folded for status reporting.

nodes.name: runResolveConflicts
nodes.summary: Interactive flow that opens the editor on conflicting hibana entries and pushes the resolved payload back to Redis.

nodes.name: runMigration
nodes.summary: Runs a planning-store migration from a source directory into the configured backend.

nodes.name: runMigrateHibana
nodes.summary: One-off migration that imports vault-stored hibana entries into Redis at a specific git commit.

nodes.name: openStore
nodes.summary: Opens the planning Redis-backed store using credentials resolved from config.

nodes.name: printStats
nodes.summary: Prints aggregate statistics about hibana and planning state for diagnostics.

nodes.name: addHibana
nodes.summary: Appends a free-text hibana note from the CLI, attaching it to the current sync state.

nodes.name: event.go
nodes.summary: Defines the append-only Event record (kind/id/text/timestamp) and its line-oriented marshal/parse routines used as the on-disk wire format for the hibana log.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses tab-separated single-line encoding with strict validation on parse to keep the log human-readable and recoverable from truncation.

nodes.name: Event
nodes.summary: Struct representing a single append-only log entry with kind (add/del), id, text payload, and timestamp.

nodes.name: ParseEvent
nodes.summary: Parses a single line of the log into an Event, rejecting malformed kinds, IDs, or timestamps.

nodes.name: event_test.go
nodes.summary: Unit tests for Event marshal/parse round-tripping, malformed-line rejection, and the empty-line sentinel behavior.

nodes.name: fake_backend_test.go
nodes.summary: In-memory fake implementation of the Backend interface used across hibana tests, with injectable failures and helper assertions over hash and graveyard sets.
nodes.languageNotes: Models the Upstash REST surface (HSet/HDel/HKeys/HMGet/SAdd/SRem/SMembers) so the same Backend interface can be exercised without network.

nodes.name: fakeBackend
nodes.summary: In-memory test double for the Backend interface backed by maps with mutex protection and an injectable one-shot failure hook.

nodes.name: fold.go
nodes.summary: Folds a sequence of append-only Events into the current set of live Notes, applying tombstones (delete) over adds, and provides recency sort.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the canonical event-sourced reduce: replay events in order, last writer wins, deleted IDs are gravestones.

nodes.name: Note
nodes.summary: Public domain object representing a live note with id, text, and creation timestamp produced by folding events.

nodes.name: Fold
nodes.summary: Reduces a list of events to live notes by tracking gravestones from delete events and skipping any add whose id has already been tombstoned.

nodes.name: fold_test.go
nodes.summary: Tests covering Fold semantics including empty input, deletes-then-adds being a no-op, edit semantics via delete+add, and recency sorting.

nodes.name: TestFoldEditViaDeleteAddPreservesCreatedAt
nodes.summary: Verifies the edit-as-delete-then-add pattern preserves the original createdAt timestamp on the resulting note.

nodes.name: id.go
nodes.summary: Generates and validates KSUID-like sortable identifiers using a 4-byte big-endian timestamp plus 6 random bytes encoded with a custom base32 alphabet.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a Crockford-style base32 alphabet without I/L/O/U for human readability and lexicographic sort order matching time order.

nodes.name: NewID
nodes.summary: Generates a new time-sortable 16-character ID by concatenating a 4-byte unix timestamp and 6 cryptographically random bytes, then base32-encoding.

nodes.name: encodeID
nodes.summary: Encodes a 10-byte raw ID into a fixed-length 16-character string using the package's custom base32 alphabet.

nodes.name: id_test.go
nodes.summary: Tests for ID length, alphabet membership, uniqueness across many calls, time-sortability, concurrent safety, and validator correctness.

nodes.name: TestNewIDConcurrent
nodes.summary: Spawns goroutines generating IDs in parallel and asserts no collisions to verify thread safety of NewID.

nodes.name: log.go
nodes.summary: Append-only file-backed event log with flock-based locking, atomic batch append, fault-tolerant read that drops trailing truncation, and tombstone-dropping compaction via temp-file rename.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses syscall.Flock for cross-process safety, fsync after writes, and rename-into-place compaction to keep the log crash-safe.

nodes.name: Log
nodes.summary: Handle to the on-disk append-only log file holding the path and a process-level mutex; the file itself is the source of truth.

nodes.name: Append
nodes.summary: Appends a single event line under exclusive flock, creating parent directories as needed, and fsyncs before releasing the lock.

nodes.name: AppendBatch
nodes.summary: Appends multiple events atomically by buffering the full payload, performing a single write under flock, and fsyncing — providing all-or-nothing semantics.

nodes.name: readEvents
nodes.summary: Streams the log line-by-line under shared flock, tolerating a single trailing truncation by silently dropping a malformed final line while surfacing mid-file corruption as an error.

nodes.name: Compact
nodes.summary: Rewrites the log dropping any add events whose ids have been tombstoned and dropping the tombstones themselves, using a temp file plus rename so a failure leaves the original intact.

nodes.name: ShouldCompact
nodes.summary: Heuristic that returns true once the log file size crosses a threshold, signaling Compact is worthwhile.

nodes.name: log_test.go
nodes.summary: Comprehensive tests for the on-disk Log including concurrent appends, truncation tolerance, mid-file corruption surfacing, atomic batch behavior, compaction correctness, and crash-safe rename semantics.

nodes.name: TestLogConcurrentAppendsArePreserved
nodes.summary: Stresses concurrent Append calls from many goroutines and asserts the file contains exactly the appended events with no interleaved corruption.

nodes.name: TestLogCompactPreservesOriginalOnTmpFailure
nodes.summary: Forces compaction to fail mid-flight and verifies the original log file is untouched, validating the temp-file-rename crash-safety contract.

nodes.name: migrate.go
nodes.summary: One-shot migrator that imports notes from legacy YAML files, a remote list backend, and a git commit fallback into the new event log, idempotently merging with a duplicate-suppression key.

nodes.name: MigrateSource
nodes.summary: Configuration struct describing where legacy notes can come from: YAML path, list backend with key, and an optional git commit reference.

nodes.name: Migrate
nodes.summary: Loads notes from the configured legacy sources, dedupes by content key against already-imported entries, and append-batches new notes into the store while reporting per-source counts.

nodes.name: MigrateLegacyBackendAdapter
nodes.summary: Adapter wrapping a legacy list-style backend so the migrator can read entries via a uniform LRange interface.

nodes.name: migrate_test.go
nodes.summary: Tests covering migration paths from YAML alone, from a list backend, the merge of YAML+list, idempotent re-runs, git-commit recovery, and graceful handling of missing git history.

nodes.name: TestMigrateRecoversFromGitCommit
nodes.summary: Sets up a temporary git repo with a commit containing legacy YAML and verifies the migrator can recover those notes when the working YAML is missing.

nodes.name: redis.go
nodes.summary: Defines the Backend interface (hash + set ops) used for remote sync and provides a no-op implementation plus an Upstash REST-API backed implementation.
nodes.languageNotes: REST backend talks to Upstash via signed HTTP requests rather than the redis wire protocol, keeping the binary dependency-free.

nodes.name: Backend
nodes.summary: Interface describing the minimal redis-flavored hash and set operations the sync layer needs against a remote store.

nodes.name: restBackend
nodes.summary: Backend implementation that issues authenticated HTTP requests to Upstash's redis REST API to perform hash and set operations.

nodes.name: do
nodes.summary: Internal helper that builds, signs, and executes a single Upstash REST request and decodes the JSON response or surfaces an error.

nodes.name: store.go
nodes.summary: Top-level Store API that ties together the event log, the Backend, and folding into a coherent CRUD surface (Add/Edit/Delete/List/Sync/Compact) for note workflows.

nodes.name: Store
nodes.summary: Public store handle composing the on-disk Log and a remote Backend, exposing user-facing note operations and sync.

nodes.name: Open
nodes.summary: Opens (and lazily initializes) a Store at the given directory wired to a Backend, expanding ~ in paths and creating the data directory if missing.

nodes.name: Edit
nodes.summary: Edits a note by atomically appending a delete-then-add pair so the new note inherits createdAt while getting a fresh ID, preserving event-log invariants.

nodes.name: List
nodes.summary: Reads all events from the log, folds them into live notes, and returns them sorted by recency.

nodes.name: MaybeCompact
nodes.summary: Triggers a log compaction only when ShouldCompact reports the file has grown past the threshold.

nodes.name: store_test.go
nodes.summary: End-to-end tests for the Store facade covering CRUD, edit semantics, persistence across instances, migration-friendly timestamps, sync, and compaction no-op behavior.

nodes.name: sync.go
nodes.summary: Bidirectional sync between the local log and a remote Backend: pushes unpushed local events, pulls remote-only adds and deletes, with a persistent pushed-set to avoid echoes and re-sends.
nodes.languageNotes: Pushed-set is persisted to disk so the convergence guarantees survive process restarts and reorderings.

nodes.name: pushedSet
nodes.summary: On-disk persistent set of event IDs that have already been pushed to the remote, used to make push idempotent across restarts.

nodes.name: Restrict
nodes.summary: Trims the persisted pushed-set down to only IDs that still exist after a log compaction, preventing unbounded growth.

nodes.name: SyncOnce
nodes.summary: Executes a single push-then-pull cycle against the remote Backend, returning a SyncReport with counts of pushed, pulled, and skipped events.

nodes.name: pushOnce
nodes.summary: Walks the local log and uploads each event that the pushed-set hasn't recorded, marking each successful push.

nodes.name: pushEvent
nodes.summary: Encodes a single event as a remote-side hash entry (or graveyard set membership for deletes) and writes it via the Backend.

nodes.name: pullOnce
nodes.summary: Reads remote hash keys and graveyard set, diffs against the local fold to find remote-only adds and deletes, and appends synthetic events into the local log without echoing back.

nodes.name: sync_test.go
nodes.summary: Extensive sync test suite covering push idempotency, edit-as-new-id, pull-only adds and deletes, no-echo guarantees, two-device convergence, push retries, offline recovery, and pushed-set restriction after compaction.

nodes.name: TestSyncTwoDeviceConvergence
nodes.summary: Simulates two devices syncing through a shared backend and asserts both converge on the same fold view after a few rounds.

nodes.name: TestSyncOfflineThenOnlineRecoversOfflineNote
nodes.summary: Adds notes while the backend is disabled, re-enables it, and verifies queued notes are pushed and visible remotely after the next sync.

nodes.name: TestCompactRestrictsPushedSet
nodes.summary: Verifies that after a log compaction the persisted pushed-set is trimmed to only ids still present in the log.

nodes.name: testhelpers_test.go
nodes.summary: Tiny package-internal helpers for constructing add/delete events at given timestamps used by the hibana test suites.

nodes.name: migration.go
nodes.summary: One-shot migration utility that imports a legacy 'leisure-vault' YAML/markdown corpus into the planning store's Redis-backed scratch, recap, and person-note keyspaces.
nodes.languageNotes: Go file with a single exported entry point that walks a directory tree and writes parsed records into the planning Store backend.

nodes.name: MigrateLeisureVault
nodes.summary: Walks a leisure-vault source directory, parses recap/notes/person files, and writes them into the planning Store via Redis, returning a structured result of imported counts.

nodes.name: MigrationResult
nodes.summary: Result struct reporting counts of recaps, person notes, and scratch entries imported by MigrateLeisureVault.

nodes.name: outbox.go
nodes.summary: Append-only on-disk outbox for buffering planning operations (writes/deletes) when Redis is unavailable; supports load and rewrite for offline/online reconciliation.
nodes.languageNotes: Mutex-guarded file-backed JSON-line log with unconditional fsync semantics.

nodes.name: OutboxOp
nodes.summary: Represents a single pending planning operation (kind, key, payload, timestamp) staged for later replay against Redis.

nodes.name: outbox
nodes.summary: File-backed append-only log of OutboxOps with locking and atomic rewrite, used by the Store to defer Redis writes when offline.

nodes.name: outbox_test.go
nodes.summary: Unit tests covering append/load/rewrite cycles, malformed-line tolerance, and sync-state round-tripping for the planning outbox.

nodes.name: reconcile.go
nodes.summary: Reconciles the local outbox against Redis on reconnect: replays append-only ops, detects blob revision conflicts, and stages or auto-resolves them via per-key conflict files.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements append-only vs blob distinction with per-key revision counters stored in Redis.

nodes.name: Reconcile
nodes.summary: Orchestrates reconciliation between the local outbox and the Redis backend, dispatching ops to append-only, blob, or recap replay paths and recording conflicts.

nodes.name: replayBlobKey
nodes.summary: Replays pending blob writes for a single Redis key, comparing local revision against remote and persisting a conflict record when they diverge.

nodes.name: ResolveBlob
nodes.summary: Force-pushes a chosen payload for a conflicted blob key, bumping the remote revision and clearing the on-disk conflict record.

nodes.name: LoadConflicts
nodes.summary: Loads all persisted Conflict records from the conflicts directory for review by the UI layer.

nodes.name: Conflict
nodes.summary: Captures a per-key reconciliation conflict (key, local payload, remote payload, revisions) for later user resolution.

nodes.name: ReconcileReport
nodes.summary: Result of a Reconcile invocation summarizing applied ops, conflicts, and remaining outbox size.

nodes.name: reconcile_test.go
nodes.summary: Tests append-only replay, blob conflict detection vs auto-push, recap conflicts, and Redis-backed usage/recap round-trip behaviour for reconciliation.

nodes.name: redis.go
nodes.summary: Defines the redisBackend interface and ships two implementations: a no-op fallback and a REST-based Upstash client used by the planning Store for persistence.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses net/http with Bearer auth against Upstash REST API; abstracts as a minimal subset of Redis verbs.

nodes.name: redisBackend
nodes.summary: Interface defining the subset of Redis operations the planning Store needs (Get/Set/Del/RPush/LRange/Incr/SAdd/SMembers).

nodes.name: nopBackend
nodes.summary: No-op redisBackend implementation returning empty/disabled results, used when no Redis URL is configured.

nodes.name: restBackend
nodes.summary: REST-based redisBackend implementation hitting an Upstash-style HTTPS endpoint with bearer-token auth for each command.

nodes.name: redis_backend_test.go
nodes.summary: Focused tests for the REST backend's handling of integer Incr results returned as strings and surfacing of error fields in responses.

nodes.name: redis_live_test.go
nodes.summary: Live integration test that exercises the REST backend against a real Upstash instance when REDIS_URL/TOKEN env vars are present.

nodes.name: redis_test.go
nodes.summary: Comprehensive Store tests against a fake redisBackend, covering plan/annotation/recap round-trips, fallback to YAML on Redis failure, and the leisure-vault migration.

nodes.name: fakeBackend
nodes.summary: In-memory test double of the redisBackend interface that records calls and supports injectable failure scenarios for individual ops.

nodes.name: store.go
nodes.summary: Central planning Store: persists plans, annotations, usage stats, recaps, and per-person notes to disk and (optionally) Redis, with a pluggable git syncer for commit/push.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses YAML for local fallback and a Redis backend for durable storage; coordinates with a Syncer for git-backed sync.

nodes.name: Store
nodes.summary: Owns a directory-backed planning store with optional Redis backend and git Syncer; exposes plan, annotation, usage, recap, and person-note APIs.

nodes.name: NewStoreWithRedis
nodes.summary: Constructs a Store wired to a Redis REST backend when URL/token are provided, otherwise falling back to the no-op backend.

nodes.name: LoadPlan
nodes.summary: Loads today's planning Plan from Redis with YAML fallback, after first triggering a git pull via the configured Syncer.

nodes.name: SavePlan
nodes.summary: Persists a Plan as a versioned blob to Redis and YAML to disk, queueing an outbox entry when Redis is unavailable.

nodes.name: Rollover
nodes.summary: Carries forward incomplete todos from yesterday's plan into today's, archiving items completed before today.

nodes.name: LogUsage
nodes.summary: Records a command-usage event by incrementing per-day Redis counters and appending an entry to the local YAML usage log.

nodes.name: LoadUsageStats
nodes.summary: Aggregates command usage from Redis (preferred) or the local YAML fallback into UsageEntry counts.

nodes.name: SaveRecap
nodes.summary: Persists a named recap document to Redis and disk, indexes it under a recap-set, and triggers a git commit/push via the Syncer.

nodes.name: ListRecaps
nodes.summary: Lists all available recap names by querying the Redis recap index with directory listing as fallback.

nodes.name: LoadAnnotations
nodes.summary: Loads issue annotations from Redis (preferred) or the local YAML file, after pulling latest from git.

nodes.name: SavePersonNote
nodes.summary: Saves or removes a per-person note (markdown) and mirrors the change to Redis when enabled.

nodes.name: store_test.go
nodes.summary: Behaviour tests for the local-disk side of the Store: plan/annotation round-trips, rollover semantics across day boundaries, usage logging, and person-note lifecycle.

nodes.name: sync_state.go
nodes.summary: Tracks per-key revision numbers seen during the last successful sync, persisted to a small JSON file alongside the outbox for use during reconciliation.

nodes.name: syncState
nodes.summary: Mutex-guarded map of key->revision numbers persisted to disk; used by Reconcile to detect blob conflicts.

nodes.name: syncer.go
nodes.summary: Defines the Syncer interface (Pull/CommitAndPush) and a default GitSyncer implementation used by the Store to keep the on-disk vault in sync with a git remote.

nodes.name: Syncer
nodes.summary: Interface that abstracts the git operations the Store relies on (pull-before-load and commit-and-push-after-save).

nodes.name: GitSyncer
nodes.summary: Default Syncer implementation that shells out to git for pull and commit/push against the planning vault directory.

nodes.name: syncer_test.go
nodes.summary: Tests the Store's interaction with a mock Syncer: that loads pull, saves commit-and-push, nil syncer is tolerated, and SyncMsg formatting is stable.

nodes.name: issue.go
nodes.summary: GitHub-issue helpers used by the ship workflow: create, validate, add to a project board, and idempotently link a sub-issue to a parent epic via the gh CLI.
nodes.languageNotes: Drives the gh CLI (REST + GraphQL) through a runner abstraction rather than an HTTP client.

nodes.name: CreateIssue
nodes.summary: Creates a new GitHub issue in the given repo via gh CLI and parses the resulting URL into an IssueRef.

nodes.name: ValidateIssue
nodes.summary: Verifies a GitHub issue exists in the target repo and returns a populated IssueRef including its node ID.

nodes.name: AddToProject
nodes.summary: Adds an issue to a GitHub Project (v2) board using the addProjectV2ItemById GraphQL mutation.

nodes.name: LinkSubIssue
nodes.summary: Idempotently links a child issue to a parent epic via GitHub's sub-issue API, returning a clear error if it is already linked under a different parent.

nodes.name: IssueRef
nodes.summary: Reference to a GitHub issue including repo, number, URL, and node ID used by the ship workflow.

nodes.name: issue_test.go
nodes.summary: Tests CreateIssue/ValidateIssue/AddToProject/LinkSubIssue against a fake gh runner, including idempotent and conflict cases for sub-issue linking.

nodes.name: fakeGH
nodes.summary: Test double for the gh CLI runner that records calls and returns scripted responses keyed by argument prefixes.

nodes.name: orchestrate.go
nodes.summary: Top-level ship workflow orchestrator that creates or attaches a GitHub issue, links it to an epic, adds it to a project board, and starts a remote tmux session.

nodes.name: Orchestrate
nodes.summary: Runs the end-to-end ship pipeline (validate-or-create issue, link epic, add to project, start session) and tolerates partial failures.

nodes.name: ResolveRepoPath
nodes.summary: Looks up the working-directory path for a given repo from a configured map, used to cd into the right checkout when starting a session.

nodes.name: OrchestrateConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration bundle for an Orchestrate invocation: repo, project URL, host, session name, and repo-path map.

nodes.name: OrchestrateResult
nodes.summary: Aggregated result of an Orchestrate run: created/attached issue, project add status, and session creation outcome.

nodes.name: orchestrate_test.go
nodes.summary: End-to-end tests of Orchestrate covering happy new-issue paths, attaching an existing issue, partial failures during session creation, and repo-path fallback.

nodes.name: runner.go
nodes.summary: Defines the GHRunner and SSHRunner interfaces and provides default implementations that exec gh and ssh respectively, enabling test injection.

nodes.name: GHRunner
nodes.summary: Interface for executing gh CLI commands with optional stdin, used throughout the ship package for GitHub API access.

nodes.name: SSHRunner

tour.title: Project Orientation
tour.description: Tack is a terminal app that helps engineers triage GitHub issues, plan work against a Notion-backed vault, and ship code through a guided workflow. Start with SETUP.md to see the configuration surface a user has to wire up (GitHub project URL, focus list, Notion/Hibana credentials), then read promote-ship-workflow.md for the end-to-end story of how an issue becomes a running tmux session on a remote dev box. Together these documents establish the user-facing narrative every code layer below ultimately serves.

tour.title: Application Entry Point and Runtime Config
tour.description: main.go is the CLI entry point: it loads config.yaml, dispatches to the Bubble Tea TUI, and also exposes side subcommands (recap/stats, conflict resolution, hibana migration). config.yaml supplies the GitHub project URL, status field name, team roster, and the focus list of issue numbers that drive what shows up on the board. Together they form the boot sequence — config loaded here flows down into every other layer in the tour.
tour.languageLesson: Go programs always start at func main() in package main. Cobra-style subcommand dispatch (TUI vs. recap vs. migration) is a common Go idiom for keeping one binary multi-purpose without splitting into multiple commands.

tour.title: Domain Model — The Vocabulary Everything Shares
tour.description: internal/model/types.go and planning.go are the most-imported files in the entire repo (fan-in 30 and 29). types.go defines Config, Project, ProjectItem, ParentRef, SubIssue, Comment, and grouping records — the shared vocabulary every package speaks. planning.go adds the Plan / FocusItem / SubItem / TodoItem / ScratchNote / MonthlyTarget structs the planning subsystem operates on. Reading these two files first means every later step refers back to types you already know.
tour.languageLesson: Go encourages plain struct types in a leaf model package with no behavior, so any layer can import them without creating import cycles. The model package here has zero outgoing edges into other internal packages — a deliberate dependency-direction choice.

tour.title: External Adapters — GitHub, Cache, Grouping
tour.description: These adapters are the boundary between tack's in-memory model and the outside world. internal/github/client.go wraps `gh auth token` and exposes GraphQL/REST helpers; queries.go hydrates a Projects v2 board into ProjectItem from Step 3, and mutations.go pushes column moves, assignments, and comments back. internal/cache/cache.go is an on-disk JSON snapshot keyed by project URL with a focus-hash guard — change your focus list in config.yaml and the cache invalidates automatically. internal/grouping/strategy.go provides the ByEpic / ByLabel pluggable groupings the board view consumes.

tour.title: Hibana — The Append-Only Event Log
tour.description: Hibana is tack's note/state engine, modelled as an event-sourced log. event.go defines the Event record (kind/id/text/timestamp) and its line-oriented marshal format, log.go is the file-backed append-only log with flock locking and tombstone-dropping compaction, fold.go folds a sequence of events into the current live notes, redis.go provides the Backend interface plus an Upstash REST implementation, and sync.go does the bidirectional remote reconciliation. id.go generates KSUID-like sortable identifiers. store.go is the public CRUD facade tying it all together.
tour.languageLesson: Event sourcing: instead of mutating a record in place, every change is an append-only Event, and current state is recomputed by folding events. Tombstones (delete events) replace destructive deletes, and compaction periodically rewrites the log to drop tombstoned entries — preserving audit history while bounding file size.

tour.title: Planning Sync — Notion-Backed Plans with Offline Tolerance
tour.description: The planning package bridges the in-memory Plan from Step 3 with a Redis-persisted, git-backed vault and Notion. store.go is the central facade for plans, annotations, recaps, and per-person notes; redis.go defines the Upstash backend; outbox.go is an append-only buffer that absorbs writes when Redis is unreachable; sync_state.go records per-key revisions; reconcile.go replays the outbox on reconnect and detects blob-revision conflicts; syncer.go defines the Syncer interface plus a GitSyncer that pulls and commits the on-disk vault. notion-integration.md explains the design and conflict semantics behind it all.
tour.languageLesson: Outbox + reconciliation is the canonical pattern for offline-tolerant clients: writes go to a local append-only log, a separate process drains them to the remote, and on reconnect a reconcile step replays buffered ops and resolves conflicts via per-key revision numbers.

tour.title: Ship Workflow — From Todo to Running Tmux Session
tour.description: The ship package implements the elevate/ship flow described in promote-ship-workflow.md from Step 1. orchestrate.go is the top-level driver: it creates or attaches a GitHub issue, links it to an epic, adds it to the project board, and kicks off a remote tmux session. issue.go has the gh-CLI helpers for creating, validating, and parenting issues. template.go renders and parses the markdown form a user fills out in their editor. session.go opens the remote tmux session over SSH (handling tilde expansion, login-shell wrapping, attach-failure tolerance). runner.go defines GHRunner and SSHRunner interfaces so all of the above can be unit-tested with injected fakes.

tour.title: TUI Core — Root Model and Board
tour.description: internal/tui/app.go is the Bubble Tea root model and the highest-fan-out file in the codebase (35). It wires together the board, plan, detail, command palette, review, and ship workflows from Step 7, and orchestrates every GitHub fetch/push and editor side-effect. board.go is the per-person grouped issue list — it consumes the GitHub data from Step 4 and the groupings from grouping/strategy.go to render expandable epics, annotations, and person notes. styles.go provides the shared lipgloss palette and the status-pill helper used across views.
tour.languageLesson: Bubble Tea uses the Elm Architecture in Go: a Model has Init, Update(msg) (Model, Cmd), and View() string. Side effects are values (tea.Cmd) returned from Update, not function calls — which is what makes the whole TUI deterministically testable.

tour.title: TUI Surface — Detail, Plan, Command, Review
tour.description: The remaining TUI panes specialize for each interaction mode. detail.go renders an issue's body and comments through Glamour with a sub-issue sidebar. planview.go is the tabbed plan view (week focus / today / hibana / scratch / monthly target) backed by the planning store from Step 6 and the hibana store from Step 5 — this is where the layers below finally surface to the user. command.go is a vim-style command palette parsing slash commands typed into the bottom prompt. review.go is the pre-quit gate that lets you toggle which queued ops actually execute, tying back to the deferred-mutation model used throughout app.go.

tour.title: Build & Dev Loop
tour.description: The Makefile closes the loop with the developer-facing build automation referenced throughout SETUP.md and CONTRIBUTING.md from Step 1: targets for building, testing, installing, and running the tack binary. AGENTS.md is included as the short orientation note that points AI agents and new contributors at the conventions you have now seen end-to-end.
tour.languageLesson: Makefile targets define build steps with dependency tracking; phony targets (test, install, run) describe non-file actions. In a Go project the Makefile is usually a thin convenience wrapper over `go build`, `go test ./...`, and `go install` — its real value is documenting the canonical commands so every contributor invokes them the same way.
